article_content: Crystal Palace aim to retain experienced assistant manager Gerry Francis as they prepare for life without Tony Pulis. The Eagles parted ways with the 56-year-old manager last week prior to their dramatic opening-day loss at Arsenal. While assistant David Kemp has exited Selhurst Park, Palace value Francis' expertise highly, especially if Tim Sherwood becomes the new head coach. Sherwood has engaged in discussions with co-chairman Steve Parish and is a betting favorite for the role. The shortlist reportedly includes Malky Mackay, who previously collaborated with Palace sporting director Iain Moody at Cardiff City. Interim coach Keith Millen managed the Arsenal match and will remain in some capacity. Palace intend to finalize their new manager within 48 hours ahead of their upcoming home match against West Ham.

article_content: Grammy-winning artist Snoop Dogg has publicly committed to ending his tobacco use, sharing on Instagram: 'Following deep reflection and conversations with loved ones, I’ve chosen to quit smoking. I kindly ask for space during this journey.' His announcement joins a growing list of influential figures who’ve successfully overcome nicotine addiction. Former U.S. President Barack Obama struggled with smoking for decades before finally quitting in 2017, crediting his wife Michelle as a key motivator. Actress Gwyneth Paltrow kicked the habit during her first pregnancy after decades of heavy use. Singer Lady Gaga recounted smoking up to 40 cigarettes daily before making a deliberate decision to stop. Jennifer Aniston credits yoga practice for helping her break a 20-year habit, while Adele relied on hypnosis after multiple relapses in 2017. These stories highlight varied pathways to quitting, emphasizing personal determination alongside specific strategies. The celebrities' experiences underscore both the challenges and possibilities of overcoming addiction, offering hope to millions worldwide.

article_content: A school inspector accused of ‘inappropriate copying and pasting’ in his reports has been dropped by Ofsted. David Marshall, a lead inspector for contractor Tribal, produced identical or near-identical sections in school assessments over three years. Ofsted halted collaboration with Marshall—also suspended by Tribal—after an investigation exposed systemic plagiarism. Similarities in his reports, first flagged in 2012, were initially deemed acceptable by Tribal. However, Ofsted now refuses to work with him due to 'new evidence.' For instance, identical phrasing described math teaching at three 2012-inspected schools, while another three schools received nearly identical wording on pupil support. Ofsted’s Matthew Coffey stated that allegations of plagiarism are taken seriously, emphasizing accuracy as a top priority. Over 60 schools in the South-East and South-West were inspected by Marshall, who previously served as a primary school head and had 13 years of inspection experience before Tribal removed his bio from its site. His dismissal follows the suspension of two other Ofsted inspectors for similar misconduct. Ofsted’s Mike Cladingbowl acknowledged past issues but denied they were routine. Critics like Civitas’ Robert Peal argued basic software could prevent such lapses, blaming contractor reliance for declining standards. Ofsted announced plans to end external contracting, managing all inspectors internally from 2024 to enhance quality control—a move Peal praised as a potential solution to 'cut-and-paste' reporting.

article_content: Software pioneer John McAfee, a fugitive from Belizean authorities, has returned to the U.S. after being deported from Guatemala. Arriving at Miami International Airport Wednesday evening, McAfee checked into a South Beach hotel. Passengers noted his tired demeanor and described him as 'calm but exhausted.' He posted on Twitter, 'I am in South Beach,' and claimed financial hardship in a blog: 'No phone, no money, no contacts.' ... Belizean police remain interested in questioning McAfee about the death of neighbor Gregory Faull but stress he is not a suspect. McAfee alleges Belizean officials sought $2M in bribes—a claim Prime Minister Dean Barrow called baseless. Guatemala detained him briefly for illegal border entry with his girlfriend, Sam Vanegas, who stayed behind.
